transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um... I hope I'm explaining this right, I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. 

I guess I came in because... well, my eating has just gotten all turned around for months now. It's probably silly, and I'm sorry if it sounds trivial, but some days I just pick at toast and coffee. And then other days... it's a bit embarrassing, actually... I'll just stand in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don't even really enjoy. I don't know why I do it. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope that's an okay place to start.
When you find yourself eating sweets in the bakery aisle, do you feel like you can't control what you're doing or how much you're eating?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really hope I didn't make it sound worse than it is. It's not like I'm... well, I'm not completely out of control or anything like that. 

I know what I'm doing, I just... I guess I just decide to buy a few things, maybe a little cake or a pastry, and I eat it. I could definitely stop if I really wanted to. I just feel a bit foolish about it, honestly, since I don't even really have much of a sweet tooth usually. 

I'm sorry if I gave you the wrong impression before. Did I answer that right for you? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things properly.
Do you feel guilty, upset, or ashamed after eating this way, especially after buying those sweets?

Oh, um... well, maybe a little bit? But really, not too much. I mean, I know I said I felt a bit foolish, but it's not like I'm sitting at home crying over a piece of cake or anything dramatic like that. 

I just think, "Oh, I probably shouldn't have spent the money on that," but then I just move on with my day. I don't let it get to me too much. It's really just a passing thought, nothing that makes me terribly upset or ashamed. 

I hope that's okay? I don't want you to think I'm making a big deal out of nothing. Am I giving you the right kind of information?
After you eat those sweets, do you ever try to make up for it by doing something like exercising a lot more than usual, making yourself vomit, or using laxatives?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I would never do anything like that. I really hope I haven't given you the idea that I'm... you know, doing things that are extreme or dangerous. 

I don't make myself sick or take any pills like that, and I'm definitely not out running miles and miles to burn off a pastry. I just... I eat it, and that's the end of it. I try to be sensible about my health, I promise. 

Does that help clear things up? I just want to make sure I'm not painting the wrong picture for you.
How often do you find yourself eating this way in the bakery aisle—like buying and eating sweets without a strong desire for them—and has this been happening for a certain amount of time?

Oh, um... let's see. It's really not that often, I promise. Maybe just... well, it's been happening for about seven months now. 

It started right around the time my aunt came to live with me. She had a bad fall, you see, and she needed some help, so she moved in. I guess since then, I just... I find myself grabbing a little something at the store every now and then. But it's not an everyday thing, I assure you! Just occasionally. 

I hope it's understandable, given the extra stress of having her there. Am I explaining that clearly enough for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
When you buy sweets in the bakery aisle, do you feel like you're eating in episodes or specific moments, and during those times, do you ever feel like you can't stop eating even if you wanted to?

Oh, no, no, it's nothing like that. I wouldn't call it an "episode," really. That sounds so... intense, doesn't it? 

It's just me standing there, looking at the display, and thinking, "Well, maybe just one." And I eat it, and then I'm done. I never feel out of control or like I can't stop. I could stop at any second if I wanted to, I just... choose to finish the little pastry. 

I'm very much in control of myself, I assure you. I don't just stand there stuffing my face without thinking! I hope that makes sense? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea about all this.
Have these eating habits affected your daily life in any way, like making it hard to focus on work, causing problems with relationships, or making you avoid social situations?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say it's ruined my life or anything like that. I really try to keep things running smoothly, I do. 

I still make sure my aunt has everything she needs, of course. I'd never let that slip. But... I suppose things have gotten just a little bit harder lately. I've missed a few of the planning calls for church, which isn't like me at all, and I've been putting off some projects for the county fair. And... well, I've had to ask the neighbors to cover a few things I usually handle on my own. 

It just feels like keeping up with my aunt's care and staying involved with everyone in town takes so much more effort than it used to. But I'm still trying my best, I promise. I hope you don't think I'm just sitting around doing nothing... am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
When you're eating those sweets in the bakery aisle or after you've bought them, do you ever feel like you can't stop eating once you start, even if you wanted to?

Oh, um... I think we might have just talked about this, right? I hope I didn't confuse you earlier. 

But no, really, I don't ever feel like I can't stop. It's truly just a small treat here and there. I'm completely in control of it, I promise. If I want to stop after one bite, I can. I just... well, I usually choose to finish it because it's already bought, you know? It would be a shame to waste it. 

I'd never let myself get carried away like that, where I couldn't stop. That sounds so frightening, and it's definitely not what's happening with me. I hope I'm being clear enough? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you ever feel distressed or significantly bothered by these eating habits, even if you don't feel guilty or ashamed right after eating?

Oh, no, not at all. I wouldn't say I'm distressed by it. It's just a little treat, you know? 

I mean, sometimes I think, "Oh, maybe I shouldn't have bought that," just because I know I don't really need the extra sugar, but... it doesn't bother me deeply or keep me up at night or anything. It's just a small indulgence to get through the grocery shopping. 

I really don't want you to think I'm upset about it or that it's some big problem. It's just a normal thing, right? Everybody likes a little something sweet now and then. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I'm trying to be as helpful as I can.
When you buy sweets in the bakery aisle, do these eating instances feel like distinct episodes — like a specific moment where you decide to eat them and then it feels like a defined event?

Oh, um... well, no, I wouldn't call them an episode or an event or anything grand like that. It's really just... well, just grabbing a cookie or a pastry while I'm walking past. 

It's not like I plan it out or make a whole big thing of it. I just see something nice, and I think, "Oh, that looks good," and I have a little bite while I finish my shopping. It's very casual, really. Just a normal part of running errands, I suppose. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm having some kind of... well, whatever an episode is. It's truly just a passing moment. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right so it doesn't sound worse than it is.
When you buy sweets in the bakery aisle, are these times when you eat them in a single, short period—like right after buying them—or do you find yourself eating them off and on throughout the day?

Oh, um... well, it's usually just right then and there. Like I said, I might just have a bite or two while I'm walking to the car, or maybe on the drive home. 

Once it's done, it's done. I don't keep going back to it all day or anything like that. I'm very good about that, really. I just have my little treat and then I move on with my day. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around eating sweets from morning till night. That would be awful, wouldn't it? 

So yes, just a quick little moment right after the store. I hope that's alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need.
When you buy sweets in the bakery aisle, is it usually because you're physically hungry, or do you sometimes eat them even when you're not particularly hungry?

Oh, I'm usually a little hungry, I think. I mean, grocery shopping takes a lot out of you, right? Walking up and down all those aisles... it's practically exercise. 

So, yes, I'd say it's just a normal little hunger pang. I wouldn't just eat something for no reason at all. I mean, I try to take good care of myself. It's just a quick pick-me-up because I've been on my feet. 

I don't just eat when I'm not hungry... that wouldn't be very healthy, would it? I hope that makes sense. I'm really trying to give you the right picture here.
When you're eating those sweets in the bakery aisle or after you've bought them, do you ever feel like you can't stop eating once you start, even if you wanted to?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. I have very good self-control, really. It's just... well, like I mentioned, just a bite or two. 

I can always stop exactly when I want to. I wouldn't just keep eating and eating without being able to stop... that sounds so frightening, doesn't it? I just have my little piece and that's the end of it. I'm very careful not to overdo things. 

I wouldn't want you to worry that I'm losing control or anything like that. I hope you don't think I have some sort of... problem with food. I'm doing alright with that, aren't I?
When you buy sweets in the bakery aisle, do you find yourself eating them very quickly, like you're rushing to finish them before you change your mind?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I rush. I mean, it's just a little treat, so I try to enjoy it, you know? 

I don't just shove it in my mouth or anything unseemly like that. I just take a normal bite... maybe chew it a little slowly, even, just to savor it. There's no hurry at all. I certainly wouldn't want to look like I'm... well, like I'm desperate for it or something. 

I just eat it at a perfectly normal pace, like anyone else would. That's the right way to do it, isn't it? I hope I'm explaining this clearly enough for you.
During these moments when you're eating the sweets you bought, do you ever feel like you're not fully in control of your eating, even just for a moment?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I'm a grown woman, I know how to control myself. 

It's really just a conscious choice to have a little treat. I wouldn't let myself just... lose control, even for a second. That wouldn't be very proper, would it? I always know exactly what I'm doing. 

I just decide to have a bite, and then I have it, and that's all there is to it. I wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of person who just lets their impulses take over. I'm keeping everything together quite well, don't you think?

Can you tell me if these times when you eat sweets from the bakery aisle happen in distinct episodes — meaning, do they feel like specific, separate instances rather than just occasional, random choices?

Oh, well... I wouldn't call them episodes. That makes it sound so serious, doesn't it? Like a medical problem or something. 

It's really just... you know, I might be walking past the bakery section on a Tuesday, and maybe I see a nice little muffin, and I just think, "Oh, I'll have that." And then maybe a few weeks later, I might get a cookie. It's just random, really. Just a little choice I make here and there. 

It's not some sort of... pattern or anything like that. Just perfectly normal, occasional choices. Anyone might do that while grocery shopping, right? I'm not doing anything unusual, am I?

Can you tell me if these times when you eat sweets from the bakery aisle happen in a way that feels like a short, specific episode — like a brief period where you suddenly decide to eat them, rather than just a normal, planned choice?

Oh, um... well, no, I wouldn't really say it's like a sudden episode or anything dramatic like that. I mean, it's just... I'll be in the store, and I'll see something nice, and I just decide to buy it. It's a perfectly normal choice, you know? 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm just acting on some strange impulse. I plan it out in my head, even if it's just a few minutes before I buy it. Like, "Oh, a piece of cake would be nice with tea later." That's how everyone shops, isn't it? Just picking up a little treat for themselves? I hope I'm making sense... I just don't want to give you the wrong impression about how I handle my groceries.
Can you tell me if you eat the sweets from the bakery aisle even when you don’t feel physically hungry at all?

Oh, well... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I wouldn't just eat something if I wasn't hungry at all. That wouldn't make much sense, would it? 

I think I just... maybe I get a little bit of a craving, or my stomach feels a little empty while I'm walking around the store. You know how grocery shopping can take a lot out of you. So I just pick up a little something because I need a bit of energy. 

I'm definitely eating because I'm hungry, even if it's just a little bit. I'm not just eating for the sake of eating. That's a normal reason to have a snack, right? I try to be very sensible about these things.
Can you tell me if there have been times when you bought and ate sweets from the bakery aisle even when you weren't physically hungry at all?

Oh, um... well, no, I really don't think so. I mean, I think we just talked about this, didn't we? I hope I'm not confusing things. 

Like I was saying, I really only get something if I'm feeling a bit peckish. It's not like I'm just stuffing my face for no reason, you know? I try to be very good about my eating habits. I wouldn't want you to think I have some kind of eating problem on top of everything else. 

I just... I listen to my body, and if it says it needs a little energy, I might get a small treat. That's the right way to do it, isn't it? Just having a snack when you're actually hungry? I'm trying my best to do the right things.
Have there been times when you bought and ate sweets from the bakery aisle even when you weren’t physically hungry at all?

I'm sorry, doctor, I... I feel like maybe I'm frustrating you, since you're asking me again. I really don't mean to be difficult, I promise. 

It's just... no, I really don't eat them if I'm not hungry. I mean, maybe sometimes it's more of an emotional hunger? Like, I just need a little comfort because everything feels so heavy and dark lately... and the voices get so loud... but I wouldn't call it eating when I'm not hungry at all. 

I'm doing my best to be healthy, I really am. I wouldn't just eat sweets for absolutely no reason. That would be gluttonous, wouldn't it? I hope you believe me that I'm trying to make good choices.
